newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN GAIN 40-RUN LEAD AGAINST SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN GAIN 40-RUN LEAD AGAINST SRI LANKA.

text.p: Sri Lanka's ace spinner Muthiah Muralitharan took a career best six for 98 but could not prevent Pakistan from gaining a useful first innings lead of 40 on the third day of their first cricket test on Monday.
Muralitharan appeared to have recovered from an injury to his hand sustained trying to take a catch on Sunday,

The leading wicket-taker of his country improved on his previous best test figures of five for 33 against Zimbabwe also in Colombo last September, by collecting his seventh five-wicket haul in a test innings.
Despite Muralitharan's superb effort Pakistan batted resolutely reaching 370 for nine at the close in reply to Sri Lanka's 330.
Ijaz Ahmed held the early Pakistan batting together with a fluent century, his seventh in test cricket.
He almost failed to make 100, however, when in a mix up with partner Salim Malik before lunch, he was first ruled run out at 98, and then recalled after the third umpire changed the earlier decision.
When Ijaz played the ball to short mid-wicket and set off for a single, Malik responded then turned back so both batsmen finished at the non-striker's end.
English umpire David Shepherd in consultation with third umpire Kandiah Francis of Sri Lanka first ruled Ijaz run out.
But when the television replays showed a sharp and clearer picture of the incident, Francis revoked his earlier decision and made Shepherd recall Ijaz and rule Malik out.
Ijaz batted 324 minutes for his 113 which included 11 fours.
Malik and Ijaz added 117 for the third wicket, before Muralitharan threatened to run through the side by snapping up three quick wickets to see Pakistan slump from 247 for three to 248 for six.
Saqlain however held the lower order together by completing his second test fifty in 255 minutes with five fours.
Sri Lanka were without left-arm fast bowler Nuwan Zoysa and Sanath Jayasuriya because of injuries.
